_doc: The client releases Fusebox speaks as. The daily client-versions workflow compares them with each client's latest release and keeps one issue open per client that is behind. A Rust test (clients.rs) checks that the constants named in `where` say the same version, so bump both together.

clients.name: Claude Code
clients.where: src/upstream.rs: CC_VERSION, CC_USER_AGENT; check the anthropic-beta list, x-stainless-* headers, cloak_body and the billing header

clients.name: Codex CLI
clients.where: src/upstream.rs: CODEX_VERSION, CODEX_USER_AGENT, CODEX_WS_BETA, CODEX_FIELD_ORDER, codex_headers; src/ws.rs for websocket messages

clients.name: Grok Build
clients.where: src/device.rs: xai::CLIENT_VERSION; src/upstream.rs: the xAI CLI-proxy headers (user agent, x-grok-*)

clients.name: Muse Code
clients.where: src/device.rs: meta::API_UA, whose build hash is the git commit compiled into the release (find it next to the version string in the macOS arm64 binary from the channel's release manifest)

clients.name: Antigravity
clients.where: src/antigravity.rs: FALLBACK_VERSION (Fusebox reads the current version from this manifest at runtime; the constant is only its fallback)
